I farm this land in a wheat-maize rotation, so I will use the full 3.8 mu for wheat in the winter season and then the same 3.8 mu for maize in the summer season. I have only 2 people in the household and 3.8 mu is not a large area, so I will keep the plan simple, stable, and yield-focused rather than complicated. Because I have 30 years of experience and well irrigation, I will rely on improved seed for wheat and hybrid seed for maize, with moderate to fairly strong fertilizer use to protect yield. For wheat, I will put more emphasis on nitrogen and phosphorus, irrigate several times because water is available and wheat responds well, and use rotary tillage because it is efficient for my scale. For maize, I will keep fertilizer balanced but slightly lighter than wheat on phosphorus, irrigate fewer times in summer, and continue rotary tillage so the work stays manageable. I will not chase extreme input levels; I will aim for steady production and lower risk.
